page: Microsoft Azure M64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1792.0 GB, yielding 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It also includes 2097 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the moderate 2.7 GHz clock speed of the Intel Xeon architecture. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and large-block uncached memory reads, achieve strong ratings in the top 25%, reaching 184.82 GB/sec and 196.25 GB/sec respectively. Other multi-core metrics, including Redis SET operations at 40.27 million operations per second and Passmark database operations, perform in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M64ms offers a highly dense memory-to-CPU configuration, making it a specialized resource for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy tasks. The high memory capacity combined with 2097 GB of local storage makes this instance well-suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise ERP applications, and data warehousing workloads that require massive RAM footprints but can tolerate moderate single-core CPU speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure M64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores running at 2.7 GHz, it features an expansive 1792.0 GB of RAM and 2097 GB of local storage. While single-core CPU benchmarks rank in the bottom 10%, its multi-core and memory subsystem performance is robust, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching a strong 196.25 GB/sec. This server is highly efficient for memory-bound applications rather than raw compute tasks. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and enterprise applications requiring massive memory density.
